title: What is A Curcumin IV | Alternative Cancer Treatment
abstract:
### Anticancer Properties  
Because curcumin is thought to have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant capabilities, experts are[exploring it as a cancer treatment](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/hp/curcumin-pdq)to help decrease swelling and inflammation related to cancer growth.  
Some studies suggest that[curcumin has anticancer characteristics](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2022.881641/full)for certain types, such as colorectal cancer. These properties include the ability to stop the cell cycle and affect cell death, inhibiting the growth of malignant cells. Curcuminoids can interfere with several cell signaling pathways to modulate cancer development.  
Studies about curcumin and cancer are still in the early stages. Formulations, doses, safety and effectiveness are still being tested in phase I clinical trials. Evidence from these pilot trials is promising, but more is needed to prove safety and effectiveness. Cancer patients should consult with their doctors before beginning any supplementary treatment options.
## Why Choose Curcumin IV Therapy?  
While you can take curcumin orally, IV delivery is recommended for faster, more direct action. Curcumin[has poor water solubility](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S177322472031371X), meaning it has a low absorption rate when passing through the digestive system. Individuals taking these supplements often[needother edible components](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7357038/)to improve bioavailability.  
With an IV injection, curcumin can bypass the gut entirely, leading to higher bioavailability. When administered under the supervision of a qualified health care professional, a curcumin IV injection optimizes absorption and potency for accelerated results. It can provide the body with immediate access to higher concentrations of curcumin’s anti-inflammatory properties and antioxidant capabilities.  
While more research is needed,[a few studies have shown](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7812094/)that curcumin may have similar effects as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and corticosteroids for certain health conditions.
